nodes.description: Homozygous or compound heterozygous NUP93 variants: missense alleles (including the European founder p.Gly591Val and the Turkish founder p.Tyr629Cys), truncating alleles, and splice variants that skip an exon. ClinGen records loss of function as the mechanism. Deleting Nup93 during mouse kidney development is embryonic lethal; that disease alleles must therefore leave residual function is a curator inference, not a published finding.

nodes.description: NUP93 is a scaffold of the inner ring of the nuclear pore complex and recruits its partner NUP205. Truncating and exon-skipping alleles fail to localize to the nuclear envelope and fail to rebuild pores in depleted Xenopus egg extracts. In a patient biopsy NUP93 staining was reduced in the nuclei of glomerular and tubular cells, and deleting Nup93 in mouse podocytes lowers nuclear pore density.
